genZNote: Koplik spots show up before the rash does — a pathognomonic early warning if you know to look for it.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human respiratory epithelium and lymphoid tissue
habitat.hostAssociation: Obligate human pathogen, no animal reservoir

identificationClues: Koplik spots (small white lesions on the buccal mucosa) are pathognomonic and precede the rash
Cephalocaudal spread of an erythematous maculopapular rash following fever and the "3 C's" (cough, coryza, conjunctivitis)
IgM serology or PCR confirms diagnosis
One of the most contagious human pathogens known, with an R0 typically cited between 12 and 18

diseases: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (rare, delayed fatal CNS complication)
Measles-associated immune amnesia (temporary impairment of pre-existing immune memory)
clinicalImportance.transmission: Airborne respiratory droplets and aerosols; extremely contagious, can remain infectious in air/surfaces for up to two hours
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Vaccine-preventable (MMR); outbreaks occur in under-vaccinated communities and can spread rapidly due to the virus's very high transmissibility
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: IgM serology is typically positive within days of rash onset; RT-PCR is used for genotyping during outbreak investigations

examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Koplik spots are a pathognomonic early clinical sign preceding the characteristic rash
